points.description: States that the compiler makes/inserts a copy of the function's code (the function body is expanded in place; inline expansion) instead of a normal call.
points.partial_credit: Half: says the function body is substituted/expanded but does not clearly say a copy of the code is made.

points.description: States that this copy is placed at every place where the function is called (each call site), i.e. the call is replaced by the code.
points.partial_credit: Half: says code is inserted at the call but not that it happens at every call.

points.description: Correctly distinguishes from a normal function call: no jump/call to a single separate copy of the function is made at run time (the call is replaced rather than executed as a call).

rubric.notes: Full marks need a precise statement that the compiler copies/expands the function code at every call site, and that this replaces the normal call. Vague wording such as "it makes it faster" or "it is treated specially" earns nothing. Any wrong statement (e.g. the function is called once and shared, or the copy is made at run time by the CPU) loses the point it affects.
